title: Deep Learning of Phase Transitions for Bilinear-Biquadratic Spin-1 Chains from Correlation Aspects
authors: Ming-Chiang Chung, Yu-Ting Kuo, Ian McCulloch, Yuan-Hong Tsai
abstract: We investigate the role of different correlation functions in reconstructing the phase diagram of the spin-1 bilinear-biquadratic chain, parametrized by the angle $θ$ between the bilinear and biquadratic couplings, using our previously developed label-free machine-learning pipeline \cite{Ming21, Ming23}, in which an autoencoder compresses iDMRG correlation matrices into latent features and K-means clustering with silhouette analysis groups them into phases. Without any prior labels, the scheme reveals four natural phases, the Haldane, dimerized, critical trimerized, and ferromagnetic phases, and accurately locates the Takhtajan-Babujian ($θ=-π/4$), $SU(3)$-symmetric Uimin-Lai-Sutherland ($θ=π/4$), and Ferro-Dimer ($θ=5π/4$) transition points; a shallow supervised refinement further sharpens the phase boundaries. We find that different correlation functions play fundamentally different roles in phase identification. The $SU(3)$-symmetric correlation alone selects a four-cluster partition that can be associated with the four phases, whereas the spin-spin and dimer-dimer correlations must be combined to recover the complete phase diagram. In contrast, the trimer-trimer correlation behaves as a marginal correlation: it is insufficient for phase identification by itself but improves the precision of the predicted phase boundaries when combined with the other correlations. Furthermore, the latent representations and silhouette values reveal signatures that we relate to the $θ$ dependence of the correlations within each phase and, tentatively, to the underlying renormalization-group structure. These results demonstrate that machine learning can not only identify quantum phases but also uncover the physical information encoded in different correlation functions.
summary: This work applies advanced machine learning techniques to map the quantum phase diagram of the spin-1 BLBQ chain. It reveals that different correlation functions encode distinct physical information, as some correlations are necessary in combination to fully delineate the known quantum phases. This demonstrates a powerful synergy between ML diagnostics and fundamental condensed matter physics.
main_problem: The study investigates how different correlation functions encode distinct physical information necessary for accurately reconstructing the complex phase diagram of the spin-1 bilinear-biquadratic chain.
main_result: The analysis shows that while the SU(3)-symmetric correlation alone can identify the four natural phases, combining spin-spin and dimer-dimer correlations is necessary for a complete picture, demonstrating the physical role of each correlation type.
method: The authors employed a label-free machine learning pipeline, using an autoencoder to compress iDMRG correlation matrices into latent features, followed by K-means clustering and silhouette analysis.
model_or_system: The system is the spin-1 bilinear-biquadratic (BLBQ) chain, governed by a Hamiltonian dependent on an angle $\theta$ that controls the relative strengths of bilinear and biquadratic couplings.
key_observables: Phase diagram regions (Haldane, dimerized, critical trimerized, ferromagnetic), correlation functions ($	ext{CSS}(r)$, $	ext{CDM}(r)$, $	ext{CSU}(3)(r)$, $	ext{CTM}(r)$), and machine learning diagnostics like silhouette values.
important_parameters: The coupling angle $\theta$, which parametrizes the phase diagram, and the specific correlation channels used as input features.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the phase structure can be robustly mapped by analyzing the geometric clustering of latent features derived from various correlation functions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram mapping out regions for different phases based on $\theta$, and show how different correlation inputs yield distinct or complementary clustering results.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the BLBQ model and its complex phase diagram, details the ML pipeline using multiple correlation inputs, presents results showing the unique contribution of each correlation function to phase identification, and concludes by relating these findings to underlying RG structures.
why_interesting: The integration of deep learning techniques (autoencoders, clustering) to diagnose fundamental physical properties like quantum phase transitions in strongly correlated quantum magnets is highly relevant for developing new computational tools in AMO and condensed matter theory.
